title: The Faceless Wedding
text: Two faceless figures stand under an arch of pale flowers, hands joined, being married. The guests have no faces either, rows of smooth heads turned politely toward the couple. As you pass, every one of them turns, and beckons you to sit.

options.label: Sit, and celebrate with the faceless. It would be rude to refuse.

outcomes.text: Good food, odd music with no singer, and little gifts for the guests. You do not ask what is in them.
You are not guests. You never were. You are the feast.

options.label: The shrewdest offers the couple a gift, and wishes them well.

outcomes.text: They are delighted, smooth heads bobbing, and show you a quick way out.

options.label: Slip away before the vows are done, before anyone asks you to stay.

outcomes.text: The music follows, and so do their smooth, turning heads, all the way to the edge of the city.
